mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if origin country is not a Hague Apostille Convention party, Spanish consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership register excerpt or equivalent UBO declaration / attribution chart
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate register, board of directors, or notary in the country of origin; if not available, a sworn corporate warranty statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where non-Hague, Spanish consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized special power of attorney for incorporation and appointment of directors (poder especial para otorgar escritura de constitución)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Spanish consular legalization; followed by official sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of each shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds statement issued by the originating bank of each shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Spanish consular legalization; official sworn Spanish translation required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and verification of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners under Ley 10/2010; screening against United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU restrictive measures, OFAC SDN list on a risk-based basis, and domestic Spanish/SEPBLAC indicators. Politically exposed persons (PEPs), family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, senior management approval, and continuous monitoring. Suspicious transactions must be reported to SEPBLAC; anti-money-laundering records must be maintained for at least ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) online service for 'certificación negativa de denominación social' — https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official language of the registry. Company names must be writable in Latin script; names in a foreign language are accepted only if necessary to describe the company object and if not contrary to public order. All corporate names will be indexed in Spanish transliteration; non-Latin UBO and director names must be transliterated using the passport/consular standard for Spanish registry and AML filings. Accents and special Spanish orthographic marks are permitted; symbols, slash marks, and misleading abbreviations are generally rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate is valid for 90 days from issuance; it cannot be administratively extended. If the deed is not executed within that period, a fresh application must be filed. On rejection or a refusal based on identity with an existing company or prohibited token, the applicant may file within one month a written recurso de alzada to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice, referencing the initial RMC application and attaching the rejected certification, alternative names, and legal grounds. If the refusal is based on a prohibited word, the applicant must first obtain the applicable ministerial authorization before resubmitting.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are acceptable for initial correspondence and registered address purposes, provided the notarial deed records the physical address of management or principal establishment if different. For a franchise licensing and syrup supply-chain entity, a purely virtual office without local management, personnel, books, or operational nexus is unacceptable for VAT registration, economic-substance expectations, and banking. It may be treated as a 'letterbox' and trigger tax anti-abuse rules, permanent establishment exposure, or denial of treaty benefits.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate risk of 30% for a newly incorporated franchise-licensing and royalty entity; risk increases to approximately 45% if only a virtual office is used with no local director, employee, or physical warehouse/contact point. SEPBLAC, the Spanish Tax Agency, and the commercial registry may carry out unannounced on-site inspections to verify real economic substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 12-14, 19-22, 23-28, 37-44, 58-61, 210-212)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Registro Mercantil Provincial del domicilio social
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) before a Spanish Notary, followed by inscripción en el Registro Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid up in cash or in-kind; cash capital must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution or Banco de España blocked account prior to deed execution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders, by unanimous written consent, resolve to subscribe and fully pay the share capital of EUR 3,000, representing 3,000 shares with a par value of EUR 1.00 each. The registered office is fixed at [Calle, Ciudad], and the company's object includes tea beverage franchise licensing, syrup production and supply. The following officers are appointed: [Name] as Sole Administrator, [Name] as Secretary (if any). The Administrator is authorized to execute the public deed, apply for the NIF, open bank accounts, and engage notaries and registrars. All appointments are accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Negative Name Certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (online via Notaría o tramitador autorizado)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names to the Registro Mercantil Central via an authorized notary or electronic window. Pay the official fee and obtain the certification proving no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The certificate is valid for three months and must be presented to the notary at the time of deed execution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the certificate is delayed, file a new application with alternative names. If the certificate expires, reapply at the same registry; no substantive cure required beyond a fresh certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Deposit of Minimum Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution or Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company account in the name of the future SL and deposit at least EUR 3,000. Obtain a certificate of deposit from the bank stating the account holder, amount deposited, and date. This certificate must be attached to the public deed. The account will be released only after the company is registered and the administrators are appointed.
required_dossiers: Proof of the legal representative of shareholders if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account opening due to incomplete entity data, correct the documentation and re-submit. If the deposit certificate is defective, request a corrected certificate from the bank before deed execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notaría) in the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders (or their attorneys-in-fact) must appear before the notary, provide the negative name certificate, bank deposit certificate, and the approved bylaws. The notary will draft and read the public deed, confirm the legality and capacity of the parties, and issue the protocol number. The deed must be signed in person or by an authorized representative, and notary fees are paid.
required_dossiers: DNI/NIE or passport of each shareholder
Power of attorney if signing by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the capital deposit, name certification, or by-laws, correct the concerned document and reschedule execution. Any rectification can be made by an addendum deed signed before the same notary without reopening the full incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax ID Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the deed is executed, submit the first copy of the deed to AEAT to obtain the provisional NIF (CIF). This number is required bank formalities and registration. The original notary copy and accompanying documentation must be presented, and the provisional NIF is issued immediately or within a few business days.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT queries the application due to missing data, resubmit the full dossier and request appointment at the relevant AEAT office. Any inconsistencies in the deed must be corrected via notarial rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Registro Mercantil Provincial
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two months from deed execution, submit a duplicate copy of the deed together with the provisional NIF and the official registration form to the Registro Mercantil. The registry examines the legality of the deed and by-laws and issues the registry entry. Once registered, the company acquires full legal personality and the definitive NIF can be requested.
required_dossiers: Second original or notarized copy of the deed
Proof of payment of the deed tax (Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados - AEDJ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a suspension note (nota suspensiva), correct the deficiencies listed and re-present the deed within the legal period (up to 60 days) either as a ratifying deed or with supplementary documents. If the registrar rejects an irrevocably defective deed, the incorporation must be repeated or corrected through a notarial rectification deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF, Social Security Registration, and Municipality Operating License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (definitive NIF); Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS); Ayuntamiento
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, request the definitive NIF at AEAT by showing the registry inscription certificate. Register the company with TGSS for social security of employee directors or staff. Before starting any activity, obtain the municipal opening license (licencia de apertura) and any business activity license (licencia de actividad) from the local Ayuntamiento, including compliance with community and urban planning rules.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription certificate (certificación del Registro Mercantil)
Lease contract of the registered office
Certificate of the registry entry for TGSS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT delays the definitive NIF, escalate to a personal appointment and present the registry certificate. For TGSS, rectify employer registration codes. For municipal license denials, submit additional technical documentation or cure by adapting the premises to the required conditions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Salud (Sanidad Ambiental) and Ayuntamiento competente; for food manufacturing, AECOSAN (Agencia Española de Consumo, Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutrición) or regional equivalent
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad y Apertura (Municipal Business Activity and Opening License) and Registro General Sanitario de Empresas Alimentarias y Alimentos (RGSEAA)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) / Regional environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full EIA required for small-scale beverage preparación; subject to municipal environmental activity license (licencia ambiental/actividad) under Ley de Evaluación Ambiental (in Catalan communities, e.g., Regimen común).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Real Decreto 140/2003 for drinking water; wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer ordinances and Real Decreto 849/1986; refrigeration systems must comply with F-gas regulation (Reglamento UE 517/2014); syrups production must meet food hygiene requirements under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 and HACCP-based controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by a qualified technician and approved by the local fire service or Ayuntamiento; structural load inspection for equipment and storage areas; workplace health and safety assessment under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica, https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; Madrid Central Office, Calle Infanta Mercedes 37.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada), the definitive NIF is granted by AEAT upon incorporation after filing Form 030 (prior declaration) and Form 036 (census filing). The SL must register in the Censo de Empresarios before beginning any economic activity and will be issued a NIF with the 'ES' VAT prefix (NIF-IVA). Foreign non-resident entities with no permanent establishment that engage in taxable Spanish supplies must file Form 036 to obtain a non-resident Spanish NIF and, if established outside the EU/EEA, appoint a tax representative recognized by AEAT (Art. 164.Dos Ley 37/1992). Registration is immediate and unconditional; there is no turnover threshold that exempts the SL from obtaining a NIF. All applications are submitted electronically using a digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN through the AEAT portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Spanish SL is a resident company subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income. No pass-through treatment is available to a standard SL. Territorial Scope: tax-resident entities are taxed on worldwide income with double-tax relief; non-resident entities are taxed only on Spanish-source income. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none at the national level; a limited special ZEC regime applies in the Canary Islands, not applicable to a mainland SL franchise business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No IRS-style check-the-box election exists in Spain. Available elections relevant to this SL: (1) consolidated tax group election under Arts. 62–75 LIS (parent owns ≥75%, group treated as one taxpayer); (2) simplified VAT regime (régimen simplificado) for enumerated retail/manufacturing activities with turnover up to EUR 250,000; (3) VAT cash-accounting scheme (criterio de caja) for SMEs with turnover up to EUR 2,000,000; (4) Patent Box election under Art. 23 LIS permitting a reduced effective rate on qualifying franchise/IP income; (5) hybrid-mismatch neutrality elections required by ATAD, applicable to franchise/royalty cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), Ley 37/1992 (LIVA); RD 1624/1992 implementing regulation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero turnover threshold: every taxable person, including the ES_SL, must register before carrying out business activity. For small-business simplified VAT regime: EUR 250,000 annual turnover in eligible activities (EUR 125,000 for agriculture). For EU remote sellers: EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold in Spain triggers registration unless the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) is used.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain imposes B2B e-invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece (Ley 18/2022); invoices must be issued/transmitted in structured XML via interoperable private platforms. The SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información del IVA) mandates near-real-time transmission of VAT invoice records to AEAT for taxpayers with turnover above EUR 6,000,000, and is obligatory for certain e-commerce operators; SII filings use Web Services/API with an XML schema (4.2) and a 4-day submission period. Under VeriFactu (RD 1007/2023), all billing software must produce verifiable invoices bearing a QR code and hash-chain digital fingerprint; the issuance timestamp and invoice data must be legally retained and made accessible to AEAT. Real-time per-invoice fiscal clearance is not generally required outside the SII framework, but non-SII taxpayers must maintain a certified billing system capable of instant AEAT inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Art. 21 LIVA to exports of tangible goods physically leaving the EU (bubble-tea syrups, equipment, packaging) provided the exporter is the consignor and holds documentary evidence of actual exit. Franchise royalties and distribution services supplied by the Spanish SL to a foreign franchisee are treated as B2B services 'effectively used and exploited' outside Spain and are outside the scope of VAT/reverse-charged in the customer's jurisdiction; intra-EU supplies of goods to a VAT-registered franchisee are zero-rated (Art. 25 LIVA) with the customer's valid VAT ID. Zero-rating is claimable only for the exact quantity that customs records prove to have left Spain/EU territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUI/SAD) filed through the Spanish DUEx customs application showing the ES_SL as exporter
Transport document of exit: Sea Bill of Lading, CMR (international road consignment note), or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Commercial invoice quoting Incoterms and stating the export sale price
Franchisee tax identification evidence (VAT registration certificate or foreign tax ID) for services and intra-EU dispatches
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103) or bank statement evidencing FX repatriation of export proceeds
Customs exit certificate 'justificante de salida' issued by the office of departure or destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT applies strict documentary audits using DUEx/ENS/EXS customs data cross-checks. Missing or fraudulent export proof retroactively converts zero-rated invoices into VAT-liable sales, triggering repayment of unused input VAT refunded, 5% annual late interest, and the recargo de apremio (5–20% late-payment surcharge). A false zero-rating claim is an infracción tributaria grave under Art. 191 LGT with penalties of 50–150% of the VAT unpaid. Forgery or simulation of export documentation with amount above EUR 120,000 constitutes a criminal tax offence under Art. 305 Código Penal, imprisonment of 2–6 years and fines of up to six times the tax amount. Additionally, if export proceeds are not repatriated to a Spanish account within 180 days, AEAT may presume disinvestment, disallow the export VAT refund, and impose exchange-control civil penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange rules are principally governed by European Union law and Spanish financial legislation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. Spain has no general exchange-control approval requirement for foreign investment, capital contributions, intercompany loans, dividends, royalties, or trade payments. Capital movements remain subject to anti-money-laundering controls, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner verification, tax documentation, statistical reporting, and applicable foreign-investment declarations. Dividend and royalty remittances may be subject to Spanish withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, or another statutory exemption. Banks may require evidence of the underlying transaction, corporate approvals, tax residence certificates, and proof of tax compliance before processing remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to Banco de España, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal repatriation deadline. Export proceeds may generally remain in euro or foreign-currency accounts and may be converted at the company's discretion. The company must retain commercial invoices, customs records, transport evidence, contracts, and payment records, and must satisfy bank transaction-monitoring and applicable statistical-reporting obligations. Cash or bearer negotiable instruments transported into or out of the European Union at amounts of EUR 10,000 or more require a customs declaration; intra-EU movements may be subject to Spanish declaration requirements where applicable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for euro-denominated payments, collections, virtual IBANs, card acquiring, and treasury interfaces where the provider is authorized by an EU or EEA competent authority and lawfully passported or established in Spain. A non-EU offshore digital EMI cannot provide regulated payment services to the Spanish company on a cross-border basis without an appropriate EU authorization, passport, Spanish establishment, or legally valid agent arrangement. EMI funds are safeguarded and are not equivalent to deposits; deposit-guarantee protection may not apply. Fintech onboarding does not eliminate Spanish AML, beneficial-owner, tax, sanctions, payment-purpose, or source-of-funds requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not universally require directors to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, certified documents, and electronic-signature processes, subject to the bank's risk policy. Banks may require an in-person meeting, notarized or apostilled documents, Spanish tax identification numbers, proof of address, a Spanish registered office, and verification of the ultimate beneficial owner where ownership, management, jurisdiction, activity, or transaction patterns create enhanced-risk indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with an opaque ownership chain or nominee arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents; current commercial-register extracts; complete ownership chart to natural-person beneficial owners; passports and proof of address; director appointment evidence; beneficial-owner declaration; notarized powers of attorney; and, where relevant, apostille, legalization, and sworn Spanish translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: New Spanish SL with no operating history, limited local substance, or expected international royalty and supply-chain payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed business plan; franchise agreements; supplier and logistics contracts; lease or registered-office evidence; staffing plan; projected monthly cash flows; expected countries, currencies, counterparties, and transaction volumes; board-approved treasury policy; and evidence of Spanish commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital from a third-party account, high-risk jurisdiction, cryptocurrency source, or unexplained foreign shareholder loan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements tracing the source of funds; audited or filed financial statements of the funding entity; shareholder resolutions; capital-increase or loan agreements; tax-residence certificates; proof of beneficial ownership; financing-purpose memorandum; sanctions screening; and independent evidence of the original wealth source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty, management-fee, or syrup-supply payments to related parties outside Spain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing analysis; invoices; proof of services or delivery; customs and transport records; intellectual-property ownership evidence; withholding-tax analysis; treaty or EU exemption documentation; economic-beneficiary confirmation; and accounting reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cash intensity, rapid pass-through flows, refunds, chargebacks, or POS collections inconsistent with the declared bubble-tea franchise model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS and acquiring contracts; store-level sales forecasts; cash-handling procedures; daily reconciliation reports; merchant statements; refund and chargeback policy; point-of-sale controls; franchisee screening files; inventory records; and management explanations for material variances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete tax identification, mismatch between corporate records and bank application, or inability to verify Spanish operating address.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NIF certificate; deed of incorporation; Mercantile Registry extract; registered-office evidence; lease or utility documentation; corporate tax registration; director and shareholder identification; and a consistency memorandum reconciling all legal names, addresses, ownership percentages, and business activities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a regulated bank using a transfer from an account held by the actual shareholder or funding entity, with an accurate payment narrative identifying equity subscription, share capital increase, or shareholder loan. For a capital increase, obtain the bank's capital-contribution certificate, execute the notarial deed, and register the increase with the Mercantile Registry. Maintain shareholder resolutions, subscription documents, source-of-funds evidence, and beneficial-owner records. Foreign direct investment and statistical filings may be required depending on investor, amount, sector, ownership, and transaction characteristics; filings should be assessed under Spanish foreign-investment reporting rules and Banco de España statistical requirements. Spanish banks may use internal purpose codes rather than a universal statutory payment-code system. Do not split transfers to avoid controls, and ensure the remitter, beneficiary, amount, currency, invoice or agreement, and tax treatment are consistent.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 cross-border payment messaging for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. Provide invoice, purchase order, contract, customs documentation where relevant, beneficiary ownership information, and sanctions-screening data. For imported syrups, packaging, equipment, or franchise-related goods, use documentary collections or a commercial letter of credit where counterparty or jurisdiction risk warrants enhanced control. A commercial LC should specify issuing and confirming banks, documentary conditions, Incoterms, shipment documents, inspection requirements, discrepancy rules, applicable UCP 600 or other agreed rules, currency, tenor, and charges. Royalty and service payments require contract, invoice, beneficial-recipient, transfer-pricing, and withholding-tax support. Banks may apply enhanced review to payments involving sanctioned, high-risk, or restricted jurisdictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank for documented forecast or committed exposures, subject to suitability, confirmations, collateral, accounting, and applicable MiFID II and EMIR requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies with restricted convertibility, where offered by an appropriately regulated counterparty and used for a genuine commercial exposure; settlement, documentation, reporting, and counterparty-risk controls are required.

Plain-vanilla currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing recurring intercompany funding or longer-term currency mismatches, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, valuation, collateral, EMIR reporting, and board-approved risk limits.
Foreign-exchange options or collars for documented commercial exposures, provided the structure is proportionate, understood by management, and not used for speculative trading.
Natural hedging through matching currency receipts and payments, currency clauses in franchise and supply contracts, and centralized treasury netting where legally and operationally documented.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts ('Depósito de Cuentas Anuales') comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, directors' report, and audit report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office (Registro Mercantil), under the General Directorate of Legal Security and Public Faith (DGSJFP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval at the Ordinary General Meeting within 6 months of fiscal year-end and deposit within 1 month of approval; outer deadline 30 July for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 60,000 per fiscal year under Art. 283 LSC; closure of the Mercantile Registry filing window ('cierre registral') for all other deeds or registrations until deposited; persistent non-filing for 3 or more consecutive years may trigger aggravated sanctions and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of statutory accounting books (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales) via the electronic e-legalización procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office; legalization section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the end of the financial year (by 30 April for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-legalized books lose evidentiary value in judicial, tax, and administrative proceedings; late legalization downgrades probative weight; administrative fines of up to EUR 1,200 may be imposed for non-legalization of commercial books.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of shareholders (Junta General Ordinaria) approving annual accounts, appropriation of profit, and discharge of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate act — not filed; recorded in the mandatory Minute Book (Libro de Actas) and notified to shareholders per Bylaws
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year (by 30 June for a calendar-year company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the ordinary meeting within the legal period exposes directors to liability under Art. 364 LSC; adoption instruments may be challenged; if losses erode equity, any shareholder can petition for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200) including tax-reconciled accounts, deductions, credits, UBO confirmation, and international transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — State Tax Administration Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month period after the tax year-end (i.e., 25 July for calendar-year taxpayers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 5% to 20% of the unpaid liability plus late-payment interest; penalties of EUR 1,000 up to 150% of the underpaid amount for inaccurate returns; defrauding tax above EUR 120,000 constitutes a criminal offense.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual informative return of transactions with third parties (Modelo 347) for suppliers and customers with aggregated annual transactions exceeding EUR 3,005 per counterparty
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the month of February of the following calendar year (1–28/29 February)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines of EUR 300 to EUR 20,000; inaccurate or omitted data penalized at 0.5% to 2% of the total omitted amount; non-filing impacts transfer-pricing documentation credibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party transaction return (Modelo 232) where related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per year or where the related-party tax regime applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month period after the tax year-end (25 July for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed penalties of EUR 1,000 to EUR 10,000 plus EUR 100 per omitted data item; transfer-pricing adjustments may be increased up to 150% if documentation is refused; evidentiary burden shifts adversely to the taxpayer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update and renewal of the franchisor registration in the regional Franchise Registry (Registro de Franquiciadores) with current franchisee network data and pre-contractual information documentation (IPRE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autonomous Community commerce authority of the registered office (e.g., Comunidad de Madrid, Generalitat de Catalunya); update announced via BORME where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the initial registration, or within the regional window (generally 1 January to 30 April) fixed by the applicable autonomous community regulation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating as an unregistered franchisor is an infringement under Ley 7/1996 de Ordenación del Comercio Minorista and regional retailer laws; fines range from EUR 600 to EUR 600,000 for serious infringements; franchise offers may be suspended and franchisees may terminate agreements with indemnity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update and reconciliation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) declaration in the Registro de Titularidades Reales (RTR) following any shareholding or control change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales (RTR) — operated by the Colegio de Registradores through the Mercantile Registry under DGSJFP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 business days of a transfer or change in ultimate ownership; the annual accounts deposit (by 30 July) operates as the annual UBO reconciliation checkpoint
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-disclosure or untimely update is an AML infringement under Ley 10/2010 with fines of EUR 600 to EUR 90,000 for minor cases and up to EUR 600,000 for serious or repeated breaches; share transfer deeds for an SL cannot be registered while RTR data is inconsistent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is mandatory for a Spanish SL when, on two consecutive balance-sheet dates, it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds: total assets greater than EUR 4,000,000; annual net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. Audit is also compulsory if the general meeting resolves it at the request of shareholders holding 5% of the share capital, or when the company is part of a group required to produce consolidated audited accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) approved by RD 1514/2007, as amended by RD 1/2021, implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS-EU mandatory for listed groups and optional for large non-listed groups; the SL prepares full, abbreviated, or micro-entity accounts depending on size and files in the Mercantile Registry's 'Normal', 'Abreviado', or 'Micro' formats.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain applies an event-driven UBO declaration model: the SL must keep an updated ownership chain, file a declaration with the Registro de Titularidades Reales (RTR) through the Mercantile Registry within 10 business days of every share transfer or change in ultimate control, and reconcile RTR data at the annual accounts deposit. Share transfers require a public deed, updating of the Libro Registro de Socios, and registration in the Mercantile Registry; the buyer may exercise company rights only after the share register is updated. For the boba franchise, ownership changes of the franchisor or master-franchisee must also be reflected in the regional franchise registry statement.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios) — mandatory under Art. 34 LSC; kept at the registered office; records shares, transfers, acquisitions, pledges and the sole-shareholder section
Minute Book (Libro de Actas) — mandatory under Art. 26 LSC; contains minutes of all shareholders' and directors' meetings

Register of Contracts with directors and sole shareholder (Libro Registro de Contratos) — mandatory under Art. 230 LSC; records contracts between the SL and its directors, affiliates and the single partner
Legalized accounting books (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales) — kept at the registered office after annual legalization by the Mercantile Registry

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 540 to 1,620 per year (approximately EUR 500 to 1,500) for a Madrid/Barcelona corporate-agent package including registered office, registered mail handling, board and compliance calendar administration; basic domiciliation in lower-cost provinces ranges from USD 320 to 540 (EUR 300 to 500).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,300 to 9,700 per year (approximately EUR 4,000 to 9,000) for a full statutory audit of a standard mid-sized Spanish SL performed by a ROAC-registered auditor; audit of a micro-entity required by a foreign parent generally ranges from USD 2,200 to 4,300 (EUR 2,000 to 4,000).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly incorporated SLs carrying on an economic activity in the first two tax years (Ley 27/2014, art. 29.1); 4% special ZEC rate for Canary Islands entities; tax credits for R&D and technological innovation (25%-42%); capitalisation reserve deduction (art. 25 LIS) of up to 10% of taxable base; deduction for reinvestment of extraordinary income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite - no statutory expiry (Ley 27/2014, art. 26); offset limited to 70% of taxable base for entities with net turnover of at least EUR 20 million, and to 50% for entities with net turnover of at least EUR 100 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 - Impuesto sobre Sociedades; filed electronically via Agencia Tributaria electronic office (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) using digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments via Modelo 202 (April, October, December) during the tax period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Twenty-five days following the six-month period after the tax year-end; for a fiscal year ending 31 December, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: NIF, legal name, registered address, tax year start/end, corporate form (SL), accounting framework, ISIC/NAICS business code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners must be identified; the Spanish SL is the filing entity and must maintain an in-country tax representative if administrative notifications are required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book profit or loss before corporate tax under Spanish GAAP, including revenue from franchise royalties, syrup supply sales, POS receipts, and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent accounting adjustments must be reconciled to Spanish GAAP; non-resident related-party transactions must be fully recorded and reconciled with the TP policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable base and adjustments (Base imponible y correcciones)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences, transfer pricing adjustments, compensation of prior tax losses, reserve deductions, and other corrections resulting in the final taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalty and service payments from the SL to a non-resident affiliate must be arm's length; documentation of the economic substance of the non-resident recipient must be retained in Spain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax liability and payment (Cuota íntegra, cuota líquida y deuda tributaria)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of 25% statutory rate, tax credits, withholdings, quarterly prepayments already made, and final amount due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents must be declared separately via Modelo 216; treaty relief or EU Directive exemptions require prior filing of Modelo 210 for refund.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of controlled transactions with related persons: franchise licence, management fees, financing, and goods supply; value, method used, and final transfer price.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent or sister company receiving Spanish royalties must furnish a Tax Residence Certificate; when thresholds exceed EUR 250,000 or turnover exceeds EUR 10 million, Modelo 232 must be filed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge (LGT art. 27): 1% per calendar month of delay up to 12 months, plus late-payment interest; after 12 months the surcharge is 15% plus late-payment interest. Penalty for non-filing or incomplete return (LGT art. 198): EUR 200 per data omission, minimum EUR 1,500. If underpayment is detected, penalty of 50%-150% of the amount underpaid. Late payment interest is currently 5% per annum in 2025 or as updated by the PGEAct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax Act (IRNR), unless reduced by treaty or eliminated under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. 0% applies for a qualifying EU/EEA parent company holding at least 10% of the Spanish SL for at least one year, with anti-abuse substance verification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority for the calendar year of payment; (2) deliver to the Spanish payer the signed TRC, a beneficial ownership statement, and, for Directive relief, evidence of the holding percentage and holding period; (3) if tax was withheld at domestic rate, claim a refund by filing Modelo 210 within four years of the date the withholding was incurred; (4) the Spanish payer must retain the documentation for possible proof before the tax administration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 19% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents resident in EU/EEA or in jurisdictions with effective exchange of information; 24% for non-cooperative jurisdictions. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, 0% applies to interest and royalty payments between associated EU companies (at least 25% shareholding maintained for at least two years). Many Spanish DTAs reduce royalty withholding to 5%-10% and interest to 0%-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File / Modelo 232 disclosure is mandatory when (a) net turnover equals or exceeds EUR 10 million, or (b) the aggregate amount of related-party transactions in the tax period exceeds EUR 250,000. Master File is required when consolidated group turnover of the ultimate parent equals or exceeds EUR 50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies substance requirements through the GAAR (art. 15 LGT), CFC rules, and TP anti-abuse provisions. A Spanish SL receiving franchise royalties or paying fees to a foreign affiliate must show real local business functions, staff and premises. A mailbox company with artificial arrangements may be recharacterized, deductions may be denied, and treaty benefits may be refused under the Principal Purpose Test.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Criminal Fraud - Art. 305 Criminal Code)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting Modelo 200 with false or incomplete data to understate taxable base: omitting POS cash sales, inflating franchise royalty deductions beyond arm's length, creating fictitious expense invoices, or shifting profits to a shell SPV with no substance. Criminal threshold: defrauding the Spanish Treasury of more than EUR 120,000 per tax type per year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 1 to 4 years, plus a fine ranging from the amount defrauded to six times that amount. If the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 600,000 or the offence is committed through interposed persons, imprisonment extends to 2-6 years and the fine is higher.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly order, consent to, or conceal the fraud are criminally liable as perpetrators. Civil liability may pierce the corporate veil under LGT Art. 42.1(a) and 42.2, making directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, interest and penalties. Travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification from management may be imposed during criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Wholly Artificial Arrangement / Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SL as a shell lacking economic substance: no employees, no physical premises, no local decision-making; using a foreign affiliate solely to channel royalty payments or brand licence fees while the intellectual property is held in a zero-tax jurisdiction without real activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterisation with upward transfer pricing adjustments, denial of royalty and interest deductions, imposition of the standard 25% tax plus late-payment interest, and penalties of 50% to 150% of the undercharged tax under LGT Arts. 191-193. Failure to comply with documentation requirements triggers additional fixed penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally created the artificial structure to evade tax are jointly liable for the hidden tax debt; in criminal cases, imprisonment applies for fraud over EUR 120,000. Travel bans and corporate veil piercing are available under LGT Art. 42.2.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Controlled Transaction Filing Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain local and master files; omitting related-party transactions from Modelo 232; charging non-arm's-length royalties or management fees to the Spanish SL; using unjustified TNMM with no benchmarking study; refusing to present TP documentation during tax inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax administration may adjust the taxable base to arm's length and issue a collection assessment. Late payment interest accrues, and penalties of up to 50% of the undercharged tax apply if the adjustment is treated as wrongful underreporting. Formal non-compliance with TP documentation carries fixed penalties under LGT Art. 198 (EUR 200 per omitted data item, minimum EUR 1,500).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed or approved false intercompany contracts and invoices can be held personally liable for the adjusted tax, interest and penalties. Where the TP adjustment arises from deliberate fraud, criminal liability under Art. 305 Criminal Code follows with imprisonment and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify and register the ultimate beneficial owner with the Registro de Titularidad Real; accepting cash payments above the statutory limit (EUR 1,000 in commercial transactions where any party is a business) and not filing a Suspicious Transaction Report to SEPBLAC; processing franchise royalty wires from sanctioned jurisdictions without adequate AML controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010 on Money Laundering Prevention: minor infringement, fine up to EUR 60,000; serious infringement, fine up to EUR 1.5 million; very serious infringement, fine up to EUR 10 million plus prohibition from operating in the sector for up to five years. If laundering is criminalised under Art. 301 Criminal Code, imprisonment ranges from 1 to 6 years and fines up to six times the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable where they knowingly failed to adopt AML/CTF procedures or consented to laundering. Criminal sanctions can be imposed directly on the director, including imprisonment, travel bans, asset freezes and disqualification from holding administrative positions in Spanish companies.
